same_element_identity_check.result: TAG LOST - a new span element replaces the old one on withdrawal, not the same DOM node

same_element_identity_check.method: tagged recognized span with data-qa-tag before Backspace, re-queried after withdrawal

notes: QA-02: both carry data-testid=natural-language-match and data-match-id. Format differs: Todoist's data-match-id is a display string ('11 Sep'); meologue's is a raw ISO date ('2026-09-11'). Already known/recorded divergence, reconfirmed.
QA-03: matched. data-highlighted-match='true' while recognised, attribute absent (not merely false) once withdrawn, in both apps.

QA-06 STRUCTURAL DIVERGENCE (new finding, contradicts the ledger's existing 'matched' status which was based only on meologue's own behaviour): Todoist does NOT keep the same span element across withdrawal - a fresh element is created (verified twice by tagging the DOM node with a custom attribute and finding it gone after Backspace, while text and visual state are unchanged). meologue DOES keep the identical DOM node (tag survives). Behaviourally indistinguishable (both restyle inline-block -> inline, padding 4px -> 0px, width delta 8px = 4+4), but structurally different at the DOM-node-identity level.
